transcript:
Header: 2027-06-30 08:42 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion InfoSec), Mark Davison (Orion Procurement), Ellen Park (Orion Cloud)

Summary: procurement review focused on MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing commitments and vendor onboarding steps. Some audio dropouts mid-call; automated transcript has small transcription errors.

00:00:00 - Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in. We'll run through the MSA/DPA ask, SLA appendix, and then pricing/onsite onboarding.
00:00:12 - Mark: Yeah thanks, we have about 45 minutes, procurement and legal will want to capture next steps, um we got a list of questions from legal earlier.
00:00:22 - Priya: Hi all, Priya here, I'm focused on data residency, encryption, KMS and the security questionnaire. I'll probably jump in a lot.
00:00:30 - Liam: Morning, Liam from Redwood, I'll cover technical bits like private deployments, VPC peering, and latency SLOs.
00:00:38 - Ellen: Ellen, cloud architect, I'll be the person implementing network and onboarding.
00:00:44 - Sofia: Great. Quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines, 2) SLA specifics (uptime & latency), 3) pricing and committed capacity / pilot, 4) onboarding timeline and required artifacts.

00:01:10 - Mark: Let's start with the MSA. Our legal sent standard redlines around liability caps and indemnities, and they asked about insurance. Can Redwood accept a 3x cap tied to annual fees?
00:01:25 - Sofia: Ok that's the usual starting point. Our standard is 1x annual subscription for liability cap but for enterprise we can talk. If this is a committed Dedicated deal, we can usually move to 2x; 3x will need exec approval. I'll flag that.
00:01:42 - Priya: Also data residency — Orion needs EU customer data to remain in eu-west-1. Does Redwood offer region pinning for Dedicated or Private?
00:01:55 - Liam: Yes, for Dedicated you can pin to a region; for Private we can deploy into your VPC on-prem or VPC in a region. There's sometimes differences in the control plane and audit log retention. Note: the transcript may say "redwood dedikated" in the doc, apologies if spelled off.
00:02:15 - Priya: Great. How do you manage key management? Our policy is customer-managed keys behind an HSM or KMS, we don't want vendor-held keys.
00:02:25 - Liam: We support customer KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. For hosted API it's vendor-managed by default, but you can buy a dedicated key option with Bring Your Own Key in some contracts. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
00:02:40 - Ellen: Network-wise we'll need VPC peering and strict egress rules, plus a list of IP ranges. Does Redwood support private endpoints or NAT-less peering?
00:02:52 - Liam: Yes, private endpoints and VPC peering are supported on Dedicated and Private. For hosted we give IP allowlists but not full peering. We'll attach our network diagram and IP range list.

00:03:20 - Mark: Ok on the SLA side, legal wants both uptime and latency SLAs. Uptime is fine, but latency is trickier. Can you commit to p50/p95 numbers for the 2k token prompt use case?
00:03:35 - Liam: We can provide reference latency numbers from our benchmark sheet — e.g., for Redwood Dedicated on A100 type GPU, p50 ~60ms per token and p95 ~120ms for typical prompt lengths, but it depends a lot on batch size and KV cache warm state. We'll send the spreadsheet.
00:03:55 - Priya: That sounds optimistic. Do you have an SLA backstop for latencies? If latency SLO isn't met, is there a credit or remediation?
00:04:06 - Sofia: Standard practice is define uptime SLA with credits; latency SLAs are often targets tied to performance profiles and we can add remediation clauses or runbook commitments for enterprise deals. We'll propose language in the SLA appendix.
00:04:22 - Mark: For procurement we need clear failure modes and credits. Also curious about fallback — if your Dedicated pool is constrained, can requests route to hosted with our data controls?
00:04:35 - Liam: We have smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants; however cross-tenant data handling differs. For strict data residency we'll not route out of region. For capacity overflow we can do burst to a controlled Hosted lane if agreed in contract — we'll note that in the appendix.

00:05:10 - Priya: Encryption in transit and at rest plus audit logs are must-haves. How long are audit logs retained and can we push them to our SIEM?
00:05:22 - Sofia: Audit logs retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private. We support log forwarding to customer SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, etc.). Default hosted retention is 90 days unless extended. We'll include the audit log options in the DPA.
00:05:38 - Priya: Ok. Also SOC2 and ISO — do you have reports?
00:05:42 - Sofia: We are SOC 2 Type II and in process for ISO27001. We'll share SOC2 report under NDA and our security pack.

00:06:10 - Mark: On pricing — procurement asked for committed capacity pricing vs on-demand. What are typical discounts for a 12-month committed Dedicated pool?
00:06:22 - Sofia: For 12-month reserved capacity we generally offer 15-30% vs on-demand depending on size; with a multi-year commit we can add more. For pilot/POC we usually run a short-term discounted pilot with a small credit balance.
00:06:40 - Mark: We need the internal approval for budgets; can we get a formal quote and a sample PO template?
00:06:47 - Sofia: Yes I'll send a formal quote and PO template. We'll also include a sample invoice cadence.

00:07:05 - Ellen: On onboarding timeline, how long from PO to production? We have compliance windows and want to minimize time to first call.
00:07:14 - Liam: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks from signed contract with network and cert provisioning; Private (on-prem) runs longer. For a pilot hosted lane, we can spin up within 2-3 days. We'll provide the onboarding checklist.
00:07:30 - Priya: For the pilot, do you allow ephemeral test data or do we need to provision synthetic data?
00:07:37 - Liam: We recommend synthetic data for initial tests; if you need production-like tests we have strict controls and can set up a dedicated pilot environment under a DPA.

00:08:05 - Speaker 1: (mumble) question about data deletion, our retention policy is 90 days, we need right to delete on request.
00:08:13 - Sofia: Yes we support delete-on-request and data retention controls in the DPA; we'll add a clause for retention and deletion timeline (recommended 30/90 days configurable).

00:08:30 - Priya: One more security item: does Redwood sign a standard DPA with subprocessors listed? We need a subprocessors list and notification window for changes.
00:08:40 - Sofia: We include a subprocessors list and we provide notice windows — typically 30 days for new subprocessors. We'll include the current list as an appendix.

00:09:05 - Mark: Legal also asked about export controls and classification of outputs — are you able to support contractual language around export compliance?
00:09:15 - Sofia: Yes we can add standard export control clauses. For certain regulated workloads we recommend Private deployment to remain air-gapped.

00:09:42 - Ellen: Technical: network egress logs and VPC flow logs — can we ingest those into our monitoring?
00:09:50 - Liam: Yes, we can push flow logs to your S3 or CloudWatch or forward to Splunk. We'll include log shipping options in the onboarding doc.

00:10:20 - Priya: About encryption keys — if we use our KMS, can we perform key rotation and still have Redwood access for inference?
00:10:29 - Liam: Yes, our integration supports key rotation; we don't hold plaintext keys. We'll document the rotation process and fallback modes.

00:10:55 - Mark: Ok, procurement process — we usually need an MSA redline and then a DPA. What's a realistic turnaround if Redwood sends redline today?
00:11:05 - Sofia: If we send redline today, legal review typically 3-7 business days, then a negotiation cycle. Given exec approvals for any liability cap uptick, plan 2-3 weeks to finalize MSA/DPA for standard enterprise deals.
00:11:20 - Mark: That fits our calendar but we need pricing sign-off by 7/15 to hit budget.
00:11:26 - Sofia: Understood — we'll prioritize the redline and the quote to try to meet that window.

00:11:50 - Speaker 2 (Priya): We have a few DPA specifics: data subject requests, breach notification timing (48 hours?), and subprocessor audit rights.
00:12:02 - Sofia: Breach notification 48-72 hours standard, but we can commit to 48 in enterprise deals. For audit rights, we provide SOC2 under NDA and customer audits for Private. We'll share options.

00:12:30 - Ellen: One friction point — our infra team wants a runbook for failover from Dedicated to Hosted in case of outages. Can you provide an example runbook?
00:12:40 - Liam: Yes, we have runbooks and can provide a sample that covers routing, cache warming (KV cash in transcript), and rollback steps. We'll sanitize it for security and attach it.

00:13:10 - Mark: On pricing again, do you do volume-based tiers for embeddings and tokens separately?
00:13:20 - Sofia: Yes embeddings and tokens are metered separately. For a Dedicated pool we can show committed token throughput and embedding throughput pricing. We'll include an itemized quote.

00:13:45 - Priya: Do you allow per-route RBAC and teams separation? We want least privilege with audit trails.
00:13:54 - Liam: We support RBAC, API keys per team, and token-level auditing in the console. You can restrict by route and model.

00:14:10 - (short pause)

00:14:30 - Sofia: Ok let's quickly go through the actual MSA redline items we flagged: liability cap, indemnity carveouts, data security obligations, and termination for convenience notice period.
00:14:42 - Mark: For termination for convenience we prefer 60 days with pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity.
00:14:52 - Sofia: Our standard is 30-90 days depending on commit; pro-rated refunds are possible but often offset by early termination fees for reserved capacity. We'll propose language.

00:15:10 - Priya: Regarding indemnity carveouts for IP claims, we need mutual indemnity for third-party IP.
00:15:18 - Sofia: We can make indemnity mutual for IP claims with typical limits. We'll add that to redline.

00:15:40 - Ellen: Tech question — do you have limits on model upload or fine-tuning? We might want to fine-tune small proprietary models.
00:15:50 - Liam: Fine-tuning is supported in Private and Dedicated with model governance features. For hosted fine-tuning we have constraints. We'll send the fine-tune policy doc.

00:16:20 - Mark: Ok, any vendor questionnaires outstanding? Priya mentioned yes.
00:16:26 - Priya: We sent an initial security questionnaire; I'd like Redwood to return answers for our legal by next week.
00:16:34 - Sofia: We'll complete that and send it back by 2027-07-02. Liam will own technical Qs.
\00:16:50 - (brief crosstalk)

00:17:10 - Liam: Quick note on performance: we rely on smart routing, quantization profiles, batching and KV cache to hit latency targets; if you have very strict p95 latency we recommend a Dedicated profile with pinned model + warm KV cache.
00:17:30 - Priya: Can you guarantee KV cache warm state? Our app has spiky requests.
00:17:37 - Liam: We can't guarantee cache warm for all spikes, but we can configure pre-warming and consistent routing strategies. We'll discuss a warm-start plan in the onboarding runbook.
\00:18:05 - Mark: For billing, do you support monthly invoicing with net-30?
00:18:11 - Sofia: Yes net-30 is standard for enterprise; we can discuss net-45/60 for certain finance approvals but typically net-30.
\00:18:30 - Priya: Anything else on compliance? We need a list of subprocessors and a data flow diagram.
00:18:36 - Sofia: We'll attach subprocessors and a redacted data flow diagram to the DPA package.
\00:19:05 - Mark: Ok this has been helpful. Let's call out explicit next steps now.
00:19:10 - Sofia: Action items: we'll send redlined MSA & DPA and the SLA appendix, Liam will send technical benchmarks and onboarding checklist, and Priya will return the security questionnaire. We'll aim to have the quote and PO template to you by 7/2 so you can route approvals ahead of 7/15.
00:19:36 - Priya: That timeline works.
00:19:40 - Ellen: Can we book the pilot onboarding slot now? Week of July 12 looks good for us.
00:19:46 - Sofia: I'll propose 2 slots in the calendar after we send the onboarding checklist.
00:19:52 - Mark: Anything else?
00:19:55 - Liam: Nothing from me, just we'll include the network diagrams and log shipping options.
00:20:00 - Sofia: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email and attach the docs.

(there's a 30-minute technical deep-dive that follows off-record; auto-transcript truncated)

51:58 - Sofia: Ok thanks again, end call.
